Using the formula: $\tan 3\theta = \frac{3\tan\theta - \tan^3\theta}{1 - 3\tan^2\theta}$.

Let $\theta = 10^\circ$:

$$\tan 30^\circ = \frac{3\tan 10^\circ - \tan^3 10^\circ}{1 - 3\tan^2 10^\circ}$$

$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{3t - t^3}{1 - 3t^2} \quad \text{where } t = \tan 10^\circ$$

Squaring both sides and simplifying:

$$3\tan^6 10^\circ - 27\tan^4 10^\circ + 33\tan^2 10^\circ = 1$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{1}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
